ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 18619, effective Nov 1, 2024) as amended, together with the Commercial Act (Act No. 17905) and the Financial Services Commission's Enforcement Decree on Beneficial Ownership Reporting. The Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) under the Financial Services Commission administers the UBO register, which is not publicly accessible but is available to competent authorities for AML/CFT purposes.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean Financial Services Commission's own sanctions list (including the List of Specified Persons under the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information). Additionally, enhanced due diligence is required for any Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) recommendations, including domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates. The screening must be conducted at onboarding and on a continuous basis using automated real-time monitoring tools, with documented escalation procedures for any positive hits. All results must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea's Online Registration System (i-REG) – 법인설립등기시스템
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Hangul (Korean script) and must include the legal form suffix '유한회사' (Yuhan Hoesa) or its English equivalent 'Co., Ltd.' to denote limited liability. An English transliteration may be registered as a secondary name, but the primary registered name must be in Hangul. The name must be unique within the same jurisdiction and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered entity. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) a distinctive element, (2) a business purpose descriptor (optional), (3) the legal form suffix, and (4) compliance with the 'Act on the Registration of Commercial Names' which prohibits names that are misleading, contrary to public order, or that imply government affiliation without authorization.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant may file a written objection with the Registry Office of the Supreme Court within 14 days of the rejection notice. The objection must state the grounds for appeal and include a revised name proposal. The Registry Office will review the objection within 10 business days and issue a final decision. If the objection is denied, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Administrative Court within 30 days of the denial. The entire appeal process typically takes 30-60 days. It is advisable to conduct a preliminary name search on the i-REG portal and to reserve the name before filing incorporation documents to avoid delays.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox arrangements are not permissible for this industry. The business scope involves refrigerated logistics warehousing for perishable pharmaceuticals, which requires a physical cold storage facility licensed by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) and the local municipal government. The tax authorities (National Tax Service) and commercial banks will reject a virtual office because the company must demonstrate a physical presence, including a registered place of business, for licensing, tax registration, and bank account opening. A physical inspection of the premises is mandatory before the issuance of the cold storage license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical on-site inspections are highly likely (estimated 80% probability within the first year of operation) by the MFDS, the National Tax Service, and the municipal fire and safety authorities. The inspection checklist includes: (1) verification of the registered office address and actual business operations, (2) compliance with cold chain temperature monitoring and recording systems, (3) proper storage conditions for pharmaceuticals, (4) fire safety equipment and emergency exits, (5) employee records and payroll compliance, and (6) tax invoice issuance and bookkeeping. The company must maintain a full-time registered agent at the physical address and ensure that all operational records are readily available for inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, December 19, 1962, as most recently amended by Act No. 17861, July 1, 2021), especially Articles 287-2 through 287-50 (yuhan hoesa limited liability company), Article 635 (application for registration of incorporation), Article 54 (registration of business office), and Article 19 (corporate capacity); also relevant provisions of the Commercial Registration Act and the Act on Registration of Real Estate and Commerce
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registry Office (Deunggi-so) under the Supreme Court of Korea, specifically the district court registry division having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, such as the Seoul Central District Court Registry Division
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Korean-language Articles of Incorporation (jeong-gwan) together with the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company filed under Article 635 of the Commercial Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea does not prescribe a minimum paid-up capital and does not require a statutory blocked escrow account for a yuhan hoesa limited liability company. However, the entire subscribed quota must be fully paid before registration into a temporary bank deposit account opened in the corporate name, and a bank certificate evidencing that deposit must accompany the incorporation registration application; funds may not be withdrawn until incorporation is registered.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION ADOPTED BY THE SOLE QUOTA HOLDER AND FIRST MEETING OF THE DIRECTORS OF YUHAN HOESA, a limited liability company to be established under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, by written resolution signed by all quota holders and directors currently entitled to vote. The meeting took place at the registered office on [Date]. The Chairman declared that a quorum was present and that all incorporators had received proper notice of the agenda. WHEREAS the Articles of Incorporation of Yuhan Hoesa and the initial corporate formation documents have been prepared; and WHEREAS for the lawful incorporation of the company it is necessary to subscribe the initial quota, adopt the registered office, appoint statutory officers, authorize opening of bank accounts, and obtain all industrial, environmental, and fire safety licenses; NOW, THEREFORE, upon a motion duly made and seconded, the following resolutions are unanimously adopted by the sole quota holder and the directors: 1. ADOPTION OF ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION. The Articles of Incorporation presented in the format required by the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, including the corporate name Yuhan Hoesa, the business purpose of refrigerated logistics warehousing and cold storage of perishable pharmaceuticals, and the initial quota capital, are approved and adopted, and the representative director is authorized to sign the Articles on behalf of all incorporators and file them with the competent court registry. 2. SUBSCRIPTION AND PAID-IN CAPITAL. The sole quota holder subscribes for the entire initial quota with a subscription price of KRW 10,000,000 or such higher amount as the bank certificate indicates. The amount subscribed has been fully paid or will be fully paid before application for registration, and the representative director is authorized to deposit the funds in a temporary bank deposit account, to receive the certificate of capital deposit, and to attach the certificate to the incorporation registration application. The funds shall not be recalled before registration. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the company is fixed at [Legal Address, District, City, Republic of Korea]. The representative director is directed to obtain from the owner or possessor of the premises a notarized letter of consent to the registered office and to file the letter with the court registry. All notices and legal process may be served at that address. 4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The representative director and the financial officer are authorized to open corporate savings and settlement accounts at any commercial bank located in the Republic of Korea, to sign ACH direct debit instructions, wire transfer remittances, bank mandate documents, corporate borrowing documents when later approved by the quota holder, and foreign exchange declarations, and to execute any corporate resolution or certificate required by such bank. This banking authority is effective from the date of this resolution until the registration of incorporation and continues thereafter for the ordinary administration of the company. 5. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The following persons are appointed as statutory officers: [Name] as Representative Director; [Name] as Auditor; and [Name] as Compliance Officer responsible for anti-money-laundering and sanctions screening. Each officer accepts the appointment and will provide an oath or acceptance statement for filing with the registry. No officer is an undischarged insolvent or otherwise disqualified under applicable Korean law. 6. STATUTORY LICENSING ACTIONS. The officers are directed to apply without undue delay for the business registration certificate with the National Tax Service, to coordinate any environmental arrangement or small-scale environmental impact assessment with the Ministry of Environment, to obtain a refrigeration plant operating approval and pressure vessel certificate from the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency, and to secure civil defense fire safety certificates and fire permits from the National Fire Agency and the local fire station. For pharmaceutical products, the officers shall also apply for the Good Distribution Practice certificate at the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety before the storage of any perishable pharmaceutical goods commences. 7. GENERAL POWER AND EFFECTIVE DATE. Each officer is vested with all powers necessary to carry out the above resolutions, including execution of applications, declarations, certificates, leases, employment agreements, and permits in the name and on behalf of the company. Expenses incidental to formation and licensing are authorized for reimbursement. This first resolution is effective upon adoption and remains in force until revoked by the quota holder. There being no further business, the meeting was adjourned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Court Registry Office (Deunggi-so) under the Supreme Court of Korea; online submission via the court e-Registry portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Coordinate with a licensed Korean notary public and the foreign or domestic incorporators. Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean containing the corporate name Yuhan Hoesa, the business purpose of refrigerated logistics warehousing and storage of perishable pharmaceuticals under ISIC 5210 and NAICS 493120, the address of the registered office, the number of quotas and the paid-in quota capital, the number of directors, the auditor provision, and the method of contribution by monetary deposit. Reserve the company name with the registry office using the court name reservation service. After name approval, notarize the Articles before a Korean notary public. Translate any foreign passports, apostilles, and powers of attorney into Korean with an affidavit of translation. Ensure that all incorporator signatures conform to their specimen seal declarations. Retain all originals and notarized copies for filing.
required_dossiers: Application for corporate name reservation
Proposed Articles of Incorporation
Passports or alien registration cards of all incorporators
Specimen seal declaration or signature card
Notarized power of attorney if any incorporator is represented
Certified translation of foreign identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the company name for similarity, file an amended name application immediately on the same or next business day. If the notary refuses notarization due to translation insufficiency, obtain a certified translation sworn by a licensed translator and resubmit within 5 business days. If the online portal rejects the application due to incomplete data, correct and resubmit within 24 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Certificate of Paid-in Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in the Republic of Korea authorized for foreign exchange banking, such as KEB Hana Bank, Shinhan Bank, or KB Kookmin Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, deliver a subscription deposit instruction to the selected bank. The sole quota holder shall deposit the total subscription price into a temporary corporate deposit account opened in the corporate name. The bank must issue a certificate of capital deposit stating the depositor, corporate name, date, amount, and account number. If funds are remitted from outside Korea, complete the foreign exchange transaction declaration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act through the bank and obtain the certificate of declaration. No blocked escrow account is required by Korean law, but the deposited funds must remain in the account until registration of incorporation. The representative director shall attach the certificate of capital deposit to the court registration application. After registration, funds may be used only for ordinary corporate purposes in accordance with the Articles.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Corporate name reservation certificate
Identification documents and seal specimen of the depositing quota holder
Capital subscription resolution
Foreign exchange transaction declaration certificate if applicable
Bank onboarding and beneficial ownership declaration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends the deposit for anti-money-laundering concerns, provide bank statements evidencing legitimate source of funds and submit a corporate beneficial ownership declaration. If the certificate is materially defective, request re-issuance within 3 business days. If the foreign exchange report is rejected, present a lawful remitter and amend the declaration before a bank officer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Registration at the Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Registry Division exercising jurisdiction over the registered office; online via the Supreme Court e-Registry portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the court e-Registry online filing function or appear in person at the district court registry. Submit the application for incorporation registration of a limited liability company under Article 635 of the Commercial Act. Attach the notarized Articles, the certificate of capital deposit, the written consent of the owner or possessor of the registered office, acceptance letters of the representative director and auditor, copies of officer identification, and proof of payment of registration tax and education surtax. The registry examiners verify the formal legality of the company name, purpose, paid-in capital evidence, address, and officer consents. Upon approval, pay the registration tax and receive the commercial register certificate evidencing legal personality. The company comes into existence on the date of registration.
required_dossiers: Application for incorporation registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of capital deposit
Consent letter of the registered-office owner or possessor
Oath or acceptance of representative director and auditor
Seal certificate of the representative director
Proof of payment of registration tax and education surtax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order, comply within 14 calendar days. If registration is refused, file a written objection with the registry chief and, if still rejected, appeal to the competent district court within one month under the Commercial Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service Business Registration and Tax Licenses
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service district tax office and local government revenue office; online via HomeTax (hometax.go.kr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 calendar days after court registration, file an application for business registration in the corporate name under the Value-Added Tax Act. Attach the commercial register certificate, the seal certificate, a copy of the lease agreement, and the representative director identification document. Select the appropriate industrial classification for warehouse and cold storage logistics, and indicate that a separate pharmaceutical distribution license will be obtained. The National Tax Service will issue the business registration certificate including a unique tax registration number. Also register for electronic tax invoice issuance and enroll as a VAT general taxpayer. Thereafter, register employees for National Pension, National Health Insurance, Employment Insurance, and Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance within the statutory deadlines.
required_dossiers: Business registration application form
Commercial register certificate
Seal certificate of the company and representative director
Representative director passport or resident identification copy
Lease agreement or proof of legal entitlement to the registered office
Statutory application for VAT general taxpayer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests clarification on the physical office, provide the electric or internet utility contract in the company name within 10 business days. If registration is filed late, pay any assessed fine promptly and submit a request for reduction under the National Tax Basic Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Environmental and Fire Safety Licensing for Cold Storage Logistics
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS); Ministry of Environment; National Fire Agency and local fire station; Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA); competent municipal and provincial logistics authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commercial operation, submit the physical site details to the appropriate authorities. Apply to the municipal or provincial government to register the facility as a logistics warehouse for refrigerated storage under the Logistics Facilities Act. For pharmaceutical products, submit a Good Distribution Practice application to the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, including temperature mapping, validation protocols, security records, and standard operating procedures for handling perishable pharmaceuticals. For refrigeration equipment and any ammonia refrigerant systems, complete the pressure vessel and special equipment inspection with the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency. Submit an environmental examination to the local environmental office to confirm whether a small-scale environmental impact assessment or only an environmental registration and exemption acknowledgment is required. Apply to the local fire station under the Fire Services Act for the fire safety permit, presenting the building construction certificate, fire suppression equipment list, and emergency evacuation plan. Obtain civil defense clearance before loading and unloading operations commence.
required_dossiers: Business registration certificate
Commercial register extract
Warehouse floor plan, architectural drawings, and refrigeration load calculations
Ammonia or refrigerant material safety data sheets
Refrigeration machinery room layout and pressure vessel test report
Wastewater and condensate discharge plan
Fire protection system design and installation certificate
Pharmaceutical GDP quality manual and validation reports for pharma operations
Logistics facility registration application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MFDS issues a deficiency letter, amend the standard operating procedures and resubmit within 15 business days. If the fire station denies the permit, engage a licensed fire safety designer and submit a revised plan within 14 business days. If the environmental office upgrades the project to a full EIA, hire an approved environmental consultant and follow the prescribed public comment and assessment schedule; otherwise consider relocating to an already licensed facility.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating through the HomeTax electronic portal (www.hometax.go.kr); customs export clearance and zero-rating evidence are administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Korean limited liability company (Yuhan Hoesa) owned by non-residents, the company must first complete its Commercial Act incorporation registration at the competent district court. The legal entity must then file an application for business registration with the local district NTS office via HomeTax within 20 days of business commencement. The filing requires articles of incorporation, certificate of incorporation, board resolution or ownership/ownership time details, evidence of the fixed place of business such as a lease contract or ownership certificate for the temperature-controlled cold storage facility, and the passport/foreign corporate certificate of the non-resident shareholders. The NTS will issue a permanent 10-digit business registration number (business operator registration number), which simultaneously functions as the VAT registration number and the corporate annual income tax identifier. For any foreign non-resident entity without domestic incorporation, a Korean tax representative must be appointed and notified to the relevant district tax office under the Framework Act on National Taxes before applying for a business registration number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Korean tax system does not provide a check-the-box-style election; a legal entity organized under the Korean Commercial Act as a Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily taxed as a corporation under the Corporate Income Tax Act, regardless of the tax classification of the entity in its home jurisdiction. Separate statutory elections are available only in specific areas such as consolidated corporate tax filing between a domestic parent and its wholly owned domestic subsidiaries, and thin-capitalization or transfer-pricing advance arrangements, but no general entity-classification election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies; every business operator carrying on a trade in the Republic of Korea is obliged to register for VAT within 20 days from the date of business commencement, regardless of annual revenue. A simplified taxpayer filing regime applies to qualifying small businesses with annual taxable revenue not exceeding KRW 80,000,000, but VAT registration remains mandatory. For foreign non-resident suppliers of remote digital services, a separate simplified VAT registration regime applies once the preceding calendar-year supply of such services to Korean customers crosses the statutory threshold set under the VAT Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All registered business operators are required to issue electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax system or through an approved e-tax-invoice program. The e-tax invoice must include the customer business registration number, supply date, supply value, VAT rate, and VAT amount. E-tax invoice data must be transmitted to the NTS by the day following the date of issuance. Cold-storage and warehousing services provided to VAT-registered customers must be covered by an electronic tax invoice; the NTS performs real-time cross-matching of declared purchases against issued invoices, and the absence of a valid e-tax invoice will deny the customer an input VAT deduction. The Korea Customs Service uses the UNI-PASS system for all export declarations, with electronic exchange of the export declaration number, and no separate physical fiscal stamp is used; anti-fraud enforcement is effected through NTS invoice matching, annual reconciliation, and penalty regimes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under the Korean VAT Act applies to goods physically exported from the Republic of Korea to a foreign country, as evidenced by an export declaration accepted by the Korea Customs Service. In the context of temperature-controlled cold storage logistics for perishable pharmaceuticals, the physical sale and delivery of the goods into Korean customs-bonded or export-procedure movement will qualify for 0% VAT only when the goods are actually exported and the foreign exchange proceeds are repatriated to Korea. Warehousing and storage services rendered to a non-resident customer in connection with goods that remain in Korea are not automatically zero-rated; such services are zero-rated only if they are supplied to a person outside Korea, are directly linked to the exported goods, and are paid for in convertible foreign currency under the foreign exchange regulations and the conditions of Article 24 of the VAT Act and its Enforcement Decree. An exporter must retain full documentary proof of physical export, foreign currency invoicing, and overseas payment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration accepted by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS system (export declaration number),
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the international carrier evidencing delivery outside Korea,
Commercial Invoice signed by the exporter and the overseas buyer,
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate or Foreign Currency Receipt Confirmation issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank,
Inward Remittance Advice / bank credit confirmation showing the export payment received from the overseas buyer,
Cold-chain temperature records and refrigerated transport logs for the perishable pharmaceutical cargo (sector-specific evidentiary support)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS has the statutory right to audit export transactions and to request the original customs declaration, bill of lading, foreign exchange bank confirmation, and payment records. If zero-rating is claimed without sufficient documentary evidence, or if export proceeds are not repatriated to Korea within the applicable foreign exchange settlement deadline (generally 180 days from export, subject to extension), the supply is re-characterized as a taxable domestic supply and the exporter becomes liable for 10% VAT on the supply value plus additional tax penalties and interest for negligent or intentional non-payment. False or fraudulent export invoices and fabricated zero-rating claims are subject to fraudulent tax invoice penalties under the VAT Act, under-assessment and tax evasion penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes, export and currency violation sanctions under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and, where the tax underpayment exceeds established thresholds, criminal prosecution sanctions may also apply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea, as the central monetary authority, operating in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; authorized foreign exchange banks administer reporting and settlement duties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized but monitoring-based foreign exchange system. Current account transactions are effectively convertible: receipts and payments for goods, services and ordinary business income may flow through licensed foreign exchange banks without individual approval. Capital account flows, however, are not unconditional; inbound foreign direct investment and outbound financial transfers require notification to the reporting authority through a designated foreign exchange bank or the Ministry of Economy and Finance. The Korean won is managed through a free-floating exchange rate regime, and there is no statutory forced surrender of export proceeds. In practice, export collections must be brought into a domestic foreign exchange bank account within settlement timeframes and can be converted to won at market rates. Profit remittance for a foreign-invested Korean LLC is lawful once corporate formalities are satisfied, but banks require proof of tax payments, audited financial documents, and an approved foreign investment report. Administrative discipline is exercised through the Foreign Exchange Information System, so wire origin and purpose codes must be clearly documented. Overall, the regime places strong emphasis on evidentiary trail rather than quantitative rationing of currency, making corporate treasury planning feasible through mainstream domestic banks rather than offshore EMIs.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Regulation on Foreign Exchange Transactions, export proceeds must be collected and repatriated into the exporter domestic foreign exchange bank account within 180 days from the shipment date unless an extended settlement period is approved by the Korea Customs Service, the Bank of Korea, or a foreign exchange bank with delegated authority. There is no mandatory conversion ratio: exporters may retain foreign currency in a designated foreign currency account or sell it to the bank in the KRW market. For cold-chain services exported to non-resident customers, the treaty trade settlement must match the declared commercial payment term and be supported by invoices, bills of lading or electronic service performance records.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and not legally viable for the Korean Yuhan Hoesa as a primary banking channel. Domestic fintech electronic money issuers licensed under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act are not full banks and cannot open a corporate foreign-invested capital escrow account or execute foreign exchange contracts under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Offshore digital EMIs without a Korean money exchange license or foreign exchange bank license are generally barred from servicing Korean entities with corporate accounts. Such providers may at most support ancillary card-issuance or payment facilitation, but the treasury for this entity must remain with tier-1 commercial banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A statutory director or formally authorized signatory must normally attend an in-person KYC interview at the chosen domestic branch to validate identity, source of funds and business purpose. While remote video interview and consular/notarized power-of-attorney documentation can streamline the process, top-tier Korean banks retain branch override rights and may require a physical presence of the foreign shareholder representative before activating foreign exchange facilities. The account opening package should therefore assume at least one authorized natural person will appear in Korea or have the relevant international apostille/consular legalization pack for the appointed corporate representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A newly formed single-member Korean LLC with non-resident shareholders presents an unclear ultimate beneficial ownership chain, especially when the cold-storage activity is cross-border.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificates of incorporation and register of shareholders of every owner in the chain; passport copies of all natural-person beneficial owners; a group structure chart showing percentage interests; a board or shareholder confirmation of beneficial ownership; Korean notarial certificate of the Yuhan Hoesa articles of association; bank reference letters from each shareholder source institution; sworn declaration of source of capital; and apostilled corporate documents for each foreign holding entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse media flags on directors or on counterparties in transshipment jurisdictions used for refrigerated cargo.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passports and tax residence certificates for all directors and signatories; joint criminal record certificates; negative media reports from a reputable international database; external sanctions/PEP screening report showing the flag and resolution; commercial contracts explaining why the flagged jurisdiction is necessary for cold-chain logistics; and a written compliance memo from the overseas AML officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial share capital and warehousing revenue sources cannot be demonstrated from verifiable independent banking records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or reviewed financial statements for the investing entity; prior-year bank statements showing accumulated cash; invoices and logistics service agreements with pharmaceutical customers; rental lease for the temperature-controlled facility; customs clearance records for refrigeration equipment; utility and refrigeration energy cost invoices; payroll register for warehouse staff; and a forward-looking business plan with profit and loss projections.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic substance mismatch where an LLC claims to conduct refrigerated logistics but lacks physical assets or staff, indicating possible trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Title deeds or executed lease agreement for the cold warehouse; registered cooling-plant purchase invoices and asset registers; engineering test certificates from the relevant refrigeration inspector; local insurance policy on the warehouse and stored pharma goods; national cold-chain logistics permit or food/medical storage license; monthly payroll and national pension records for employees; and a statement of actual directors operations schedule.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder should file a foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act with a domestic foreign exchange bank or KOTRA. After the report is granted, capital must be remitted through an international bank wire using the shareholder's own account in the country of origin. The SWIFT MT103 must include the approved report number as reference, and a clear purpose code corresponding to equity capital for a logistics enterprise. On receipt, the Korean bank credits the capital escrow account and later issues the foreign investment certificate after verifying the remittance, share issuance and valuation. Capital verification is satisfied by the bank's receipt confirmation and a certified capital verification memo prepared by the Korean CPA. The LLC cannot rely on crypto, cash deposits or money service businesses to complete its initial FDI injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational treasury uses SWIFT MT103 credit transfers for supplier payments and service fees through the chosen foreign exchange bank. For cold-chain equipment purchases, a commercial letter of credit advised through the Korean bank is preferred when the counterparty requires a bank undertaking. A documentary collection under URC 522 can be used for lower-value temperature-controlled packaging. Domestic ACH direct and Korean financial network transfers are used for KRW-denominated local payroll, utilities and tax payments. All foreign currency outflows must be coded with the appropriate Foreign Exchange Transactions Act purpose code and supported by invoices, contracts and import declarations where applicable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable KRW/USD forward contracts executed only with the licensed foreign exchange bank and supported by underlying cold-chain equipment import invoices or trade invoices.
FX swap contracts limited to cash-flow matching for parallel import/export receivables and payables, not for speculative open positions.
Vanilla FX options bought for downside protection on non-KRW revenue receipts, subject to the banks real-demand verification.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) may be used only for offshore hedging by the non-resident shareholder where Korean entity cannot economically access onshore liquidity; this remains a residual tool and requires prior approval under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Financial Statements for the immediately preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year ending 31 December: file no later than 31 March of the following calendar year. If the company does not have a 31 December fiscal year, file within three months of the fiscal year end. A one-month extension is available only upon pre-filed application with tax security.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 20 percent of the unpaid corporate tax amount (40 percent in cases of intentional misstatement or concealment), plus delinquency interest accruing at 0.022 percent per day until fully settled. Continued non-payment can trigger tax seizure and administrative strike-off of the company through the Commercial Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Surcharge Return and Payment (Korean local income tax on corporate net income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial, City, or County Government (Local Tax Office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the corporate income tax deadline: 31 March for a 31 December fiscal year. Payment is remitted to the local government where the registered office is located.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquency penalty equal to 20 percent of the unpaid local surcharge plus daily delinquency interest of 0.022 percent. Local government may enforce attachment or cancellation of business licenses for logistics or cold storage operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For the first half of the calendar year (January through June): file by 25 July of the same year. For the second half (July through December): file by 25 January of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underreporting penalty of 10 percent of the unpaid VAT, escalated to 20 percent for deliberately fraudulent returns, plus daily delinquency interest at 0.022 percent. Repetitive non-filing may result in forced assessment and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members and Approval of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registrar of the district court with jurisdiction over the registered office (resolutions are registered for public record when required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The regular general meeting of members must be convened within three months after the fiscal year end; for a 31 December fiscal year, this means by 31 March. Financial statements and distribution proposals must be presented for approval at that meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Convening a members' meeting late is an administrative offence punishable by a fine not exceeding KRW 10 million under the Commercial Act. Resolutions requiring registry filing that are filed late trigger a separate daily administrative fine of KRW 10,000 per day after the 14-day filing window.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Auditor Appointment and Audit Report Filing (if compulsory audit threshold applies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service / National Tax Service (the auditor must be registered under the Act on External Audit of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The independent auditor must be appointed within four months from the beginning of the fiscal year, and the completed audit report must be available no later than the date of the regular general meeting; if the meeting is held on 31 March, the report is due by that date and must be attached to the tax return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A company that is subject to mandatory external audit and fails to obtain an audit report risks a fine of up to KRW 30 million and invalidation of the submitted financial statements for corporate tax purposes. The auditor also cannot be changed without reporting to the Financial Supervisory Service if the first audit is omitted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry Amendment Filings for changes in members, managers, registered capital, or registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registration Office, Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea (subject to local district registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each change in members, managers, capital, or address must be registered within 14 days of the occurrence of the change; if the change requires prior government approval, the 14-day period runs from the date of approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register a required change triggers a daily administrative fine of KRW 10,000 under Article 635-4 of the Commercial Act, and interested persons may be denied legal standing in third-party disputes until the change is registered.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the statutory framework of the Act on External Audit of Companies as enforced in the Republic of Korea, an independent certified public accountant audit is compulsory if any of the following applies: (1) the company's total assets as of fiscal year end are at least KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 8.8 million); (2) the company is a licensed refrigerated logistics warehouse for pharmaceuticals designated by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety and has annual gross revenue exceeding KRW 5,000,000,000 (approximately USD 3.7 million) or holds a bonded cold storage permit requiring audited accounts; (3) the company has been designated a public-interest or 'large-scale' logistics enterprise by the Financial Services Commission and meets the asset threshold of KRW 7,000,000,000 combined with two consecutive years of KRW 10,000,000,000 in revenue; or (4) the company voluntarily opts for an external audit to meet financing, insurance, or licensing conditions. There is no general headcount trigger for a private Yuhan Hoesa, but a cold chain operator with more than 100 employees and total assets above KRW 3,000,000,000 may be regarded as a public-interest entity if it stores controlled pharmaceutical products.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared under Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) when the company is subject to mandatory external audit. For non-audited private limited liability companies, the company may prepare financial statements under Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles for non-public entities (K-GAAP for Small and Medium Companies). If the enterprise is a licensed pharmaceutical cold storage facility, the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety additionally requires accounting records to be prepared in a manner consistent with its Inspection and Certification Guidelines, and the financial statements must be readable by the supervisory authorities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not maintain a separate annual UBO registry filing for a private Yuhan Hoesa, but the company must keep a current and complete register of its members and beneficial owners at its registered office. Any transfer of a membership interest takes effect upon payment of consideration and approval by the members, and such transfer must be reflected in the member register immediately. Where a foreign investor acquires at least KRW 100 million of equity, the transaction must be reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act within 30 days of the acquisition through a designated foreign exchange bank or the KOTRA investment reporting portal. At every annual general meeting, the managing persons must confirm that the member register and beneficial ownership records match the latest share registry and must record changes in the minutes. After any transfer, the amended member list must be filed with the Commercial Registry within 14 days; failure to update the internal register is an administrative violation punishable by a fine.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,400 - USD 2,800 per year for a professional registered office and corporate agent in Seoul or Busan, including correspondence handling and service of process, but excluding notary fees for amendment filings
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 - USD 30,000 per year for a mandatory external audit if the company breaches the KRW 12 billion total asset threshold, or if the cold chain warehousing license requires audited financials; US 3,000 - 8,000 for a voluntary review-level engagement when no statutory audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal national corporate income tax rate for taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; below the threshold, rates are 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% up to KRW 20 billion and 21% up to KRW 300 billion.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Free Economic Zone and Free Trade Zone cold-chain logistics operators may obtain 50%-100% corporate income tax exemption or reduction for 3-5 years under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act; qualifying R&D expenditure on temperature-control software, automation, and energy efficiency may attract a preferential R&D tax credit of up to 20%-50%; investment tax credits are available for qualifying cold-storage facility equipment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Return (Form No. 10) filed via the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal; all mandatory attachments, including non-resident schedules and transfer pricing forms, are submitted with the same e-filing package.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return, accompanied by semi-annual provisional corporate tax prepayments during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The final return is due within three months after the close of the fiscal year (for a calendar-year taxpayer, March 31 of the following year); when the return is prepared and signed by a certified tax accountant, the filing deadline is extended by one month to the fourth month after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Entity Identification and Non-Resident Shareholder Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business registration number, tax office, ISIC 5210 industry code, authorized share capital, fiscal year dates, and election boxes for foreign-owned enterprise, non-resident-controlled entity, and free zone operator status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List every non-resident beneficial shareholder and its tax residence country, ownership percentage, Tax Residency Certificate reference, and foreign address. Do not report the non-resident shareholder's foreign income in this return; the Korean Yuhan Hoesa is taxed as a resident company on its worldwide income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Gross Operating Revenue and Intercompany Turnover
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue from temperature-controlled storage, pharmaceutical cold-chain logistics, handling fees, and ancillary warehouse services, shown in KRW.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If revenue was generated under contracts with a non-resident parent or affiliate, disclose the transaction values as booked and attach the transfer pricing schedule. Where the intercompany tariff deviates from independent third-party cold-storage market rates, the National Tax Service will impute arm's-length revenue and impose additional tax. Maintain temperature logs, bills of lading, warehouse entry records, and foreign-exchange receipts as contemporaneous support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Deductible Expenses and Non-Resident Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs such as labor, power, rent, repairs, depreciation, insurance, licensing fees, and intercompany management, interest, and royalty expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduction of payments to non-residents is denied unless the payee's economic substance, actual service provision, arm's-length pricing, and Korea withholding tax compliance are evidenced. Attach the outbound remittance schedule, show the statutory or treaty withholding rate applied, and confirm that Tax Residency Certificates and beneficial ownership declarations are on file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Taxable Income, Progressive Tax Rates and Local Surtax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of tax base after non-deductible items, loss carryforwards, exemptions, and free-zone incentive deductions; application of the progressive corporate income tax schedule and the 10% local income tax surcharge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For reduced FEZ/FTZ rates, complete the exemption schedule and attest that all core income-generating activities - refrigerated warehousing, inventory management, and risk assumption - are physically performed in Korea. If the corporate board has no Korean substance, the National Tax Service may deny the exemption as a sham. Use the top statutory marginal rate for provisional tax instalments to avoid underpayment penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Foreign Tax Credit and Treaty Relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Creditable foreign taxes on foreign-source income included in the Korean corporate tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For Korean tax paid on domestic-source income to a non-resident, treaty relief is not reported on this line; instead, the withholding payer must apply the DTA rate at source. For foreign withholding taxes suffered by the Korean entity on foreign cold-chain income, claim a foreign tax credit limited to the Korean corporate income tax and local surtax attributable to that foreign-source income. Retain the foreign tax receipts and tax returns for at least five years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Non-Resident Remittance and Withholding Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of dividends, interest, royalties, management fees, rent, and other domestic-source income paid or credited to non-residents during the fiscal period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare each payee's jurisdiction, gross amount, treaty rate claimed, tax withheld, and the identity of the actual beneficial owner. If a payment was made to a non-resident without withholding and without an approved DTA reduction, the Korean payer is liable for collection of the 22% statutory withholding tax, plus penalties and interest. False declaration of treaty entitlement is treated as fraudulent omission and may trigger criminal prosecution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a non-filing additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; unfaithful or under-reported returns attract 10%-20% additional tax, and deliberately false returns attract up to 40%; delayed tax payments incur daily late-payment interest. Where evasion is committed by fraudulent acts, the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act imposes imprisonment of up to 3 years or a fine of up to three times the evaded amount; in aggravated economic crimes above statutory thresholds, imprisonment may be enhanced and the responsible directors may face personal asset seizure and travel blacklisting.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge) on dividend distributions, including deemed profit repatriation, to non-resident shareholders; bilateral treaty reductions are available only after procedural DTA relief is approved.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before remitting dividends, interest, or royalties, the Korea payer must obtain from the non-resident beneficial owner: (a) a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the home jurisdiction tax authority for the relevant year; (b) a completed Application for Tax Exemption or Reduction under a Tax Treaty (Form No. 24) filed with the National Tax Service or delivered to the withholding payer; and (c) written evidence that the non-resident is the actual beneficial owner, not a conduit, and will not onward-transfer the income to an ineligible resident of a third country. The reduced treaty rate may be applied at source; otherwise 22% is withheld and the non-resident must seek a refund through the National Tax Service. Beneficial ownership must be demonstrated by business purpose, control, ownership of the claim, and full assumption of risk related to the underlying income.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on cross-border royalties and intercompany interest is 22% (20% national plus 2% local). Under many Korean bilateral tax treaties, the rate is reduced to 0%-15% for interest and 10%-15% for royalties; typical United States-Korea treaty practice applies 10% to interest and qualifying industrial royalties. Claiming the reduced treaty rate requires submission of the Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership declaration, and documentary proof that the royalty or interest amount is arm's-length and economically connected to active cold-storage or financing activity.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5,000,000,000 (KRW 5 billion) in aggregate cross-border related-party transactions triggers mandatory Local File and, where the foreign group has consolidated revenue exceeding KRW 100 billion, Master File preparation; an International Transaction Summary Report and transfer pricing method disclosure must also be filed under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although Korea has not adopted Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations, the Korean tax law applies the substance-over-form doctrine, the OECD Multilateral Instrument principal-purpose test, and general anti-avoidance rules to deny treaty and incentive benefits where the entity lacks genuine business purpose. For a refrigerated logistics company, the Core Income-Generating Activities must be performed in Korea: physical cold-storage capacity, qualified local staff, commercial risk, client contracts, daily temperature-control operations, and strategic board decisions. A Yuhan Hoesa whose board, treasury, contracts, and management decisions occur outside Korea and that merely holds title to a warehouse will be reclassified as a shell and lose tax treaty and free-zone incentive protection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Income Omission
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting cold-storage rental and handling revenue received from a foreign parent, recording below-market intercompany storage fees without business justification, or routing payments through a shell entity in Hong Kong, Belize, or the BVI to evade Korean corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 9(1) of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act: imprisonment for up to 3 years or a fine of up to 3 times the amount of tax evaded; additional tax of 20% for unjustified under-reporting under Article 47-4 of the Framework Act on Taxes; local income tax surcharge and daily delayed-payment interest are collected on top of the reassessed national tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where corporate formalities are used as an instrument of fraud, the National Tax Service and courts pierce the corporate veil and hold the representative director jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax, penalties, and local surcharges; criminal conviction may result in imprisonment, confiscation of personal and foreign assets, travel blacklisting, and seizure of bank and investment accounts held in the director's name.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Economic Substance Abusive Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare and submit the Local File, Master File, and International Transaction Summary Report where cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion; fabricating a guaranteed-cost-plus arrangement that shifts all risk and profit to a tax-haven foreign parent while the Korean entity retains only legal title to refrigerated assets and no commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs for non-submission of documentation and false reporting, plus reassessment using the best method selected by the National Tax Service; non-arm's-length income adjustments are taxed at source with 10%-20% under-reporting additional tax and interest; intra-group service and royalty deductions are denied where service value is not substantiated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause the submission of false transfer pricing documentation may be prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act; personal asset restitution may be ordered, and directors may be declared jointly liable for the adjusted corporate tax, with travel bans and criminal imprisonment of up to 3 years in willful evasion cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion and Treaty Abuse on Outbound Dividends, Interest, and Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring and remitting dividends, interest, or royalties to a non-resident without withholding the statutory 22% or an approved treaty-reduced rate, and using a letter-box company in a treaty jurisdiction to manufacture residence or beneficial ownership and bypass the Korean source withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Korean payer is liable to collect the unwithheld 22% national and local tax; under the Corporate Tax Act and Local Tax Act, the withheld tax is recovered from the payer together with negligence additional tax of up to 20% and daily late-payment interest; treaty reduction is denied ex post and the funds are reassessed with an additional 40% false-claim penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director and finance officers who directed the non-withholding or treaty abuse are personally jointly liable for the unpaid corporate and local withholding taxes; criminal indictment under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may impose imprisonment, asset freezing, confiscation of foreign accounts, and blacklisting; civil actions by the state may attach the directors' personal real estate, vehicles, and pension assets to satisfy the tax claim.
